edition.sessionCovered: Thu, Oct 29 close (PCE day) / Fri, Oct 30 early
edition.stripNote: Fri 30 Oct. September PCE +0.5% m/m — hottest since March. Q3 GDP 3.4%. VP Vance writes to Iran's Rezaei. OPEC+ meets Nov 1. US midterms Nov 3. $11B BTC options expiry today.
edition.scoreboardCaption: Fri 30 Oct early vs Thu 29 close. Ranked best to worst.
edition.commodleHint: VP Vance wrote to Iran's Rezaei seeking a _____ to de-escalate the Hormuz conflict

overview: The September PCE inflation print — 0.5% month-over-month, the hottest since March — dominated market sentiment on Friday, reinforcing the case for a December rate hike and pushing the implied probability to roughly 87%. Gold slid 0.8% to $4,005, testing the psychologically important $4,000 support level, as the 10-year Treasury yield held near 5% and Q3 GDP printed a strong 3.4% initial estimate. Silver tumbled 2.7% to $52.20, extending its worst month in over a year. Brent crude eased 0.3% to $114.20 and WTI to $101.80 after reports that VP Vance wrote to Iran's Mohsen Rezaei seeking to revive ceasefire talks — but Tehran called a Qatari-mediated draft proposal 'unacceptable,' and October closed with an estimated 30 or more shipping attacks near the Strait of Hormuz. OPEC+ meets Sunday and the US midterms are Tuesday.

Platinum posted its steepest single-session decline in weeks, falling 3.3% to $1,485, as the hot PCE data lifted real yields and crushed rate-sensitive metals. Palladium slipped to $1,000. Copper fell 1.2% to $6.58/lb as the stronger dollar offset mine supply support. Newcastle coal firmed to $151.50 as European TTF natural gas topped €100 per MWh for the first time since late 2022, boosting coal-switching demand. Bitcoin fell to $79,200 as $11 billion in Deribit options expired with max pain around $78,000; Ethereum dipped to $2,270. Chinese lithium carbonate pulled back to ¥99,500, slipping below the ¥100,000 level it had briefly reclaimed earlier in the week. Soybeans edged up to 1,232¢ on export demand, while corn held flat at 452¢ and wheat eased to 598¢. Cocoa firmed to $5,511 on Ivory Coast supply concerns.

watchItems.title: OPEC+ meets Sunday, November 1
watchItems.text: OPEC+ convenes Sunday with Brent above $114 and Hormuz disruptions tightening physical markets. The cartel faces a dilemma: compliance with voluntary cuts is high and geopolitical supply losses support prices, but the hot PCE reading and December rate-hike expectations threaten demand. Whether the group signals a willingness to ease voluntary cuts ahead of Tuesday's US midterms will set the tone for oil into year-end. The meeting also follows reports that Washington told Gulf states to prepare for a possible military campaign after the elections.

watchItems.title: US midterm elections November 3
watchItems.text: Tuesday's midterms could reshape Washington's approach to the Iran-Hormuz conflict. Reports indicate the US has told Gulf states to prepare for a possible short, intense campaign against Iran after the vote, while VP Vance's letter to Iran's Rezaei opens a separate diplomatic track. Control of Congress affects defense budgets, sanctions authority, and the legislative path for any Iran settlement. Markets are also watching whether election results change the dynamics of US engagement in the broader Middle East conflict.

watchItems.title: Gold tests $4,000 as yields stay elevated
watchItems.text: Gold at $4,005 sits just $5 above the psychologically critical $4,000 level, the floor since August. The hot September PCE (+0.5% m/m), the 10-year yield near 5%, and a December hike probability now at 87% are all headwinds. A decisive break below $4,000 could trigger technical selling toward the $3,900 zone. Silver's 17% October decline and platinum's 14% drop suggest the precious metals selloff has further to run if inflation stays sticky.

watchItems.title: European gas TTF above €100/MWh
watchItems.text: European TTF natural gas topped €100 per MWh for the first time since late 2022, driven by Hormuz disruption to Qatari LNG flows and below-average storage heading into winter. The spike supports Newcastle coal — up 40% year-to-date — and feeds into European inflation, complicating the ECB's December rate decision. JKM Asian LNG spot near $31.80 per MMBtu reflects the global energy supply squeeze. Higher gas prices also raise the risk of industrial demand destruction in Europe.

desk.name: Gold
desk.sum: Gold fell 0.8% to $4,005 on Friday, testing the $4,000 support level for the first time since August. The September PCE inflation print at 0.5% m/m — the hottest since March — reinforced the case for a December rate hike and pushed the implied probability to 87%. Q3 GDP came in at a strong 3.4% initial estimate. The 10-year Treasury yield held near 5%. The metal is now about 29% below its January record near $5,608.

desk.name: Silver
desk.sum: Silver tumbled 2.7% to $52.20 on Friday, extending its steepest monthly decline in over a year. The metal is down about 17% in October as the hawkish Fed, hot PCE data, and rising real yields hammered precious metals. The gold-silver ratio widened to approximately 76.7, reflecting silver's deeper underperformance.

desk.name: Oil
desk.sum: Brent eased 0.3% to $114.20 on Friday after reports that VP Vance wrote to Iran's Mohsen Rezaei seeking ceasefire talks, trimming some of the Hormuz risk premium. WTI dipped to $101.80. However, Tehran called a Qatari-mediated draft proposal 'unacceptable,' and October closed with an estimated 30 or more shipping attacks — the highest monthly total since tracking began. Goldman Sachs estimates about $7/bbl of the current price reflects elevated war-risk shipping costs. OPEC+ meets Sunday.

desk.name: Copper
desk.sum: Copper fell 1.2% to $6.58 per pound on Friday as the stronger dollar and hot PCE data weighed on base metals. The Yangshan copper premium hit a record $200 per tonne, signalling tight physical supply in China. However, the macro headwinds from December hike expectations and the firmer dollar are outweighing supply support in the near term.

desk.name: Coal
desk.sum: Newcastle coal firmed 0.5% to $151.50, supported by European TTF natural gas topping €100 per MWh for the first time since late 2022. The gas-to-coal switching economics continue to favour coal in Asia and Europe. The IEA forecasts record global coal demand of 8.94 billion tonnes this year. Indonesia's production shortfall and the Hormuz LNG disruption keep the supply side tight.

desk.name: Platinum
desk.sum: Platinum plunged 3.3% to $1,485 on Friday — its worst session in weeks — as the hot September PCE data lifted real yields and crushed rate-sensitive metals. The metal is down 14% on the month. WPIC's forecast of an 18% drop in total platinum demand this year continues to cap rallies, and the December hike probability at 87% adds further downward pressure.

desk.name: Palladium
desk.sum: Palladium fell 1.5% to $1,000 on Friday, hitting the round-number support level. The metal is down about 23% on the month. Platinum substitution in gasoline catalysts and growing EV market share continue to structurally weigh on demand. Aerospace and superalloy end-uses provide a floor.

desk.name: Hormuz Terminal
desk.m: ~30 transits/day vs 85 pre-war · ~30 attacks in Oct
desk.sum: October closed with an estimated 30 or more confirmed attacks on shipping near the Strait of Hormuz — the highest monthly total since the Washington Institute began tracking. VP Vance wrote to Iran's Mohsen Rezaei seeking ceasefire talks, and Qatari mediators presented a draft proposal to Tehran, but Iran called it 'unacceptable.' Meanwhile, reports indicate Washington has told Gulf states to prepare for a possible short, intense military campaign after the November 3 midterms. UKMTO has logged over 140 conflict-related incidents since February 28. OPEC+ meets Sunday.

desk.name: Corn
desk.sum: December corn was flat at 452 cents on Friday, largely unmoved by the PCE data or oil market developments. Managed money still holds substantial short positions in corn. The US corn harvest is nearing completion at roughly the five-year average pace.

desk.name: Wheat
desk.sum: December wheat eased 0.5% to 598 cents on Friday, ending October down about 16% on the month. Record managed-money short positions and adequate global supply continue to weigh on prices. The stronger dollar and hot PCE data provided no support. Winter wheat planting remains on schedule across the US Southern Plains.

desk.name: Soybean
desk.sum: November soybeans rose 0.8% to 1,232 cents on Friday, finding modest support from export demand. The US harvest continues to run ahead of the five-year average, pointing to a large crop. Brazilian production estimates remain robust, but near-term Chinese buying interest provided a floor.

desk.name: Cryptocurrencies
desk.sum: Bitcoin fell to $79,200 on Friday as approximately $11 billion in options expired on Deribit, with the max-pain level around $78,000 pulling prices lower. The hot PCE data and 87% December hike probability weighed on risk assets. The $79,500 support zone that analysts flagged ahead of the expiry did not hold cleanly. Ethereum dipped to $2,270. Markets now look to the US midterms on Tuesday and the OPEC+ meeting Sunday for the next directional catalyst.

desk.name: LNG
desk.sum: Asian LNG spot (JKM) edged higher toward $31.80 per MMBtu as European TTF natural gas topped €100 per MWh for the first time since late 2022. Hormuz disruption continues to threaten Qatar's 106 million tonnes of annual LNG export capacity. Henry Hub eased to $3.02. The wide gap between US domestic and global spot markets persists, and below-average European storage heading into winter supports the bull case.

desk.name: Sulfur
desk.sum: Sulfur remains elevated with CFR Southeast Asia around $1,100–1,300 per tonne, little changed on the week. Middle East FOB prices hold near $765. Hormuz disruption continues squeezing sulfuric acid supply chains — the essential input for copper leaching, phosphate fertilizer, and oil refining. Chinese sulfuric acid (98%) trades near 1,647 yuan per tonne per NBS data.

desk.name: Potash
desk.m: Down from $396 in Jul · China port MOP ¥2,898
desk.sum: Muriate of potash (MOP) CFR Brazil holds near $367 per tonne, little changed. Chinese domestic port MOP remains near 2,898 yuan per tonne. Belarus and Russia still account for about 40% of global supply despite Western sanctions, routing through non-aligned buyers. Seasonal fertilizer demand in the Southern Hemisphere provides modest support.

desk.name: Antimony
desk.sum: Chinese antimony (#1 ingot) held near 90,000 yuan per tonne, consolidating after October's correction from the 105,000 yuan post-holiday high. Supply remains structurally tight with China's Document No. 46 export controls limiting shipments of antimony trioxide and related compounds. Demand from flame retardant and PV glass sectors is subdued, capping the upside.

desk.name: Gallium & Germanium
desk.m: China exports −94% since controls · domestic Ga ~¥1,740/kg
desk.sum: Gallium remains near a record $1,850 per kilogram outside China, up over 200% since early 2025. Chinese domestic gallium trades near 1,740 yuan per kilogram. Beijing's Document No. 46 export controls retain a presumption of denial for US end users, and the Busan truce's Document No. 72 suspension has not meaningfully restored exports. China produces about 98% of global gallium and 60% of germanium.

desk.name: Vanadium
desk.sum: Vanadium pentoxide (V₂O₅) holds near $5.02 per pound, slipping from $5.44 in 2024 as steel demand softens. The long-term bull case rests on vanadium redox flow batteries (VRFBs) for grid-scale energy storage, but the timing of large-scale adoption remains uncertain. China, Russia and South Africa control over 90% of supply.

desk.name: Cocoa
desk.sum: ICE cocoa firmed 0.9% to $5,511 per tonne on Friday. Rising Ivory Coast arrivals — up nearly 20% in the current marketing year — and ICE inventories at a 2.25-year high continue to cap rallies, but El Niño forecasts affecting West African producers into 2027 provide support. The cocoa market remains volatile with prices well off the $12,931 record.

desk.name: Cobalt
desk.sum: Cobalt traded at $34,620 per tonne, flat on the day but down about 12% on the month. The DRC (70% of global mine supply) maintains export quotas of 96,600 tonnes per year to support prices, but the EV battery chemistry shift from NMC to LFP continues to structurally reduce demand. Aerospace and superalloy uses provide a floor.

desk.name: Lithium
desk.sum: Chinese lithium carbonate spot pulled back 0.6% to ¥99,500 per tonne, slipping below the key ¥100,000 level it had briefly reclaimed earlier in the week. SMM's weekly review flagged softening spot transactions and recycled material prices under pressure. Futures remain near ¥94,000, roughly halved from the mid-May peak above ¥200,000. Goldman Sachs projects the global market flipping from a 404,000-tonne deficit in 2026 to a 444,000-tonne surplus by 2028.

desk.name: Rubber
desk.sum: Natural rubber (RSS3) trades around $2,550 per tonne ($2.55/kg), little changed. Southeast Asian supply remains tight with Thailand, Indonesia and Malaysia — producing 70% of global latex — still affected by fungal leaf blight (Pestalotiopsis). Auto-sector demand remains solid, supported by replacement-tyre cycles.
